items.title: Nirvana Upon Rebirth, and the Opening of Nirvana Without Effort

items.zh: 云何生般涅槃補特伽羅？謂纔生彼已，便般涅槃。是名生般涅槃補特伽羅。云何無行般涅槃補特伽羅？謂生彼已，不起加行、不作功用、不由勞倦，道現在前而般涅槃。
items.en: What is a practitioner attaining final nirvana upon rebirth? It is one who, no sooner having been reborn there, attains final nirvana. This is called a practitioner attaining final nirvana upon rebirth. What is a practitioner attaining final nirvana without effort? It is one who, having been reborn there, without arousing special exertion, without applying particular effort, without any real toil, has the path manifest before them and attains final nirvana.

items.zh: 是名無行般涅槃補特伽羅。

items.title: Section: Nirvana Through Genuine Effort, and Ascending Through the Heavens

items.zh: 云何有行般涅槃補特伽羅？謂彼生已，發起加行、作大功用、由極勞倦，道現在前而般涅槃。是名有行般涅槃補特伽羅。云何上流補特伽羅？謂有不還補特伽羅，從此上生初靜慮已，住於彼處，不般涅槃。從彼沒已，展轉上生諸所生處，乃至或到色究竟天，或到非想非非想處。是名上流補特伽羅。
items.en: What is a practitioner attaining final nirvana through effort? It is one who, having been reborn there, arouses real exertion, applies great effort, and, through genuine toil, has the path manifest before them and attains final nirvana. This is called a practitioner attaining final nirvana through effort. What is a practitioner who ascends to a higher realm? It is a non-returner who, having been reborn in the first absorption, dwells there without attaining final nirvana, and who, upon dying there, passes progressively upwards through successive rebirths, until reaching either the Highest Form Heaven or the Sphere of Neither Perception nor Non-Perception. This is called a practitioner who ascends to a higher realm.

items.title: Section: Time-Liberated — Five Grades of Arhat Whose Freedom Depends on Conditions

items.zh: 云何時解脫補特伽羅？謂有補特伽羅，鈍根種姓，於諸世間現法樂住容有退失，或思自害、或守解脫，勵力勤修不放逸行。謂防退失增上力故，或唯安住自分善品；或經彼彼日夜、剎那、瞚息、須臾，勵力勝進，乃至未證最極猛利。是名時解脫補特伽羅。
items.en: What is a time-liberated practitioner? It is one of dull-facultied disposition, whose meditative ease in this very life remains genuinely susceptible to relapse — who may contemplate self-harm [rather than be overcome by the obstacles to concentration], or may guard their liberation, or may strive diligently in conduct free of heedlessness. This is called a time-liberated practitioner.

items.title: Unshakeable Attainment: Liberation Independent of Circumstance

items.zh: 云何不動法補特伽羅？謂有補特伽羅，與上相違，當知是名不動法補特伽羅。
items.en: What is a practitioner of unshakeable attainment? It is one who is the direct opposite of what was just described — know that this is called a practitioner of unshakeable attainment.

items.title: Section: Wisdom-Liberated and Both-Liberated Complete All Twenty-Eight Types

items.zh: 云何慧解脫補特伽羅？謂有補特伽羅，已能證得諸漏永盡，於八解脫未能身證具足安住。是名慧解脫補特伽羅。云何俱分解脫補特伽羅？謂有補特伽羅，已能證得諸漏永盡，於八解脫身已作證具足安住，於煩惱障分及解脫障分心俱解脫。是名俱分解脫補特伽羅。
items.en: What is a wisdom-liberated practitioner? It is one who has already permanently exhausted every outflow, yet has not yet fully realised and dwelt within the eight liberations through direct experience. This is called a wisdom-liberated practitioner. What is a both-liberated practitioner? It is one who has already permanently exhausted every outflow, and has fully realised and dwells within the eight liberations through direct experience — a mind liberated with respect to both the portion belonging to the obstruction of affliction and the portion belonging to the obstruction of concentration. This is called a both-liberated practitioner.

items.title: Section: Establishing Practitioners — Eleven Principles Behind the Twenty-Eight Types

items.zh: 云何建立補特伽羅？謂由十一差別道理。應知建立補特伽羅。云何十一差別道理？一、根差別故；二、眾差別故；三、行差別故；四、願差別故；五、行迹差別故；六、道果差別故；七、加行差別故；八、定差別故；九、生差別故；十、退不退差別故；十一、障差別故。
items.en: How are practitioners classified? By eleven distinct principles should the classification of practitioners be understood. What are the eleven distinct principles? First, difference of faculty; second, difference of assembly; third, difference of temperament; fourth, difference of vow; fifth, difference of practical approach; sixth, difference of path-fruit; seventh, difference of effort; eighth, difference of concentration; ninth, difference of rebirth; tenth, difference of retrogression versus non-retrogression; eleventh, difference of obstruction.

items.title: Faculty and Assembly Close Briefly; Temperament Reopens With the Desire-Type's Visible Signs

items.zh: 云何由根差別建立補特伽羅？謂根差別故，建立二種補特伽羅。一者、鈍根，二者、利根。云何由眾差別建立補特伽羅？謂眾差別故，建立七種補特伽羅。謂比丘、比丘尼、式叉摩那、勞策男、勞策女、近事男、近事女。云何由行差別建立補特伽羅？謂行差別故，建立七種補特伽羅。謂若貪增上補特伽羅，名貪行者。若瞋增上補特伽羅，名瞋行者。若癡增上補特伽羅，名癡行者。若慢增上補特伽羅，名慢行者。若尋思增上補特伽羅，名尋思行者。若得平等補特伽羅，名等分行者。若薄塵性補特伽羅，名薄塵行者。問：貪行補特伽羅應知何相？答：貪行補特伽羅，於諸微劣所愛事中，尚能生起最極、厚重、上品貪纏，何況中品、上品境界。又此貪纏住在身中，經久相續，長時隨縛。由貪纏故，為可愛法之所制伏，不能制伏彼可愛法。諸根悅懌、諸根不強、諸根不澀、諸根不麁，為性不好以惡身語損惱於他，難使遠離、難使厭患，下劣勝解，事業堅牢、事業久固，禁戒堅牢、禁戒久固，能忍能受。於資生具為性耽染，深生愛重，多喜多悅，遠離顰蹙，舒顏平視，含笑先言。如是等類，應知是名貪行者相。
items.en: How does difference of faculty classify practitioners? By difference of faculty, two kinds are established: the dull-facultied and the sharp-facultied. How does difference of assembly classify practitioners? By difference of assembly, seven kinds are established: monks, nuns, female probationers, male and female novices, and male and female lay disciples. … Question: What marks should one recognise in a desire-type practitioner? Answer: A desire-type practitioner, even towards the most trivial objects of attachment, can still generate the most extreme, heavy, superior-grade entanglement of desire — how much more so towards middling or superior objects. This entanglement, moreover, lodges within them, continuing without break, binding them over a long time. Through this entanglement, they are overcome by whatever is attractive, unable to master it in turn. Their faculties are pleasant and at ease, neither rigid, nor coarse, nor harsh; they are, by nature, disinclined to harm others through unwholesome speech or action; they are difficult to separate from desire, difficult to bring to genuine disgust with it, and of inferior conviction [in the Dharma]; their undertakings are steady and enduring, their discipline steady and enduring; they are able to bear hardship and endure it; towards the necessities of life they are, by nature, deeply attached, holding them dear; they are frequently joyful and cheerful, free of a furrowed brow, open-faced, direct in gaze, smiling and speaking first. All such traits together should be recognised as the marks of a desire-type.

items.zh: 問：瞋行補特伽羅應知何相？答：瞋行補特伽羅，於諸微劣所憎事中，尚能生起最極、厚重、上品瞋纏，何況中品、上品境界。又此瞋纏住在身中，經久相續，長時隨縛。由此瞋纏，為可憎法之所制伏，不能制伏彼可憎法。

blocks.text: The remaining types of non-returner and arhat, then the eleven principles by which all twenty-eight are classified.

Some attain final nirvāṇa **upon rebirth** in a higher heaven; some **without effort** (Master Cháng Bǎi: not that they don't practise, only that no special exertion is needed); some **through effort**; some **ascending** through successive heavens to the highest form heaven or the peak of existence.

"One of dull faculties, whose meditative ease in this very life remains susceptible to relapse." Venerable Miào Jìng: five varieties: retrogressing, contemplating self-harm, guarding, abiding, advancing. Master Cháng Bǎi: concentration sometimes lapses but, guarded, reappears.
The opposite: liberation independent of circumstance.
**Wisdom-liberated**: all corruptions exhausted, but the eight liberations not yet realised in person. **Both-liberated**: liberated both from affliction and from the obstruction to concentration.

The twenty-eight types are classified by eleven differences: faculty, assembly (monks, nuns, probationers, novices, lay followers), temperament, vow, practical approach, path and fruit, practice, attainment, rebirth, retrogression, and obstruction.

The desire-type is recognisable: "even towards the most trivial objects", desire is heavy and long-lasting. Yet "their faculties are pleasant and at ease, neither rigid nor coarse"; they are not inclined to harm others; their undertakings and discipline are "steady and enduring"; they are cheerful, "free of a furrowed brow, open-faced", but hard to turn away from desire. Master Cháng Bǎi: because of attachment, they can keep at something for a long time.

quiz.q: What is nirvāṇa upon rebirth, and who is reborn where, according to Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: attaining nirvāṇa as soon as reborn there; a third-fruit noble one reborn in the form realm soon gives rise to the path
quiz.why: "It is one who, no sooner having been reborn there, attains final nirvana." Master Cháng Bǎi: a third-fruit noble one, just reborn in the form realm, soon gives rise to the noble path, cuts the remaining afflictions, and enters nirvāṇa.

quiz.q: The note says nirvāṇa "without effort" is nearly automatic, with no special striving at all. What do the masters say?
options: Cháng Bǎi: not no practice, just no special exhausting effort; Miào Jìng: practice still happens, only easily and freely
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: it is not that one does not practise at all, only that no special exertion or exhausting effort is needed. Venerable Miào Jìng: "without toil" still means practising, just easily, freely, without hardship.

quiz.q: The ascending practitioner reaches either the Highest Form Heaven or the peak of existence. How does Venerable Miào Jìng distinguish the two?
options: those who love wisdom reach the Highest Form Heaven; those who love concentration go to the formless realm
quiz.why: "Passing progressively upwards through successive rebirths, until reaching either the Highest Form Heaven or the Sphere of Neither Perception nor Non-Perception." Venerable Miào Jìng: those who love wisdom attain nirvāṇa at the Highest Form Heaven; those who love concentration go on to the formless heavens.

quiz.q: What marks a time-liberated practitioner, and what does Master Cháng Bǎi say can be lost?
options: dull by disposition, their present meditative ease can lapse; what lapses is concentration, not the path
quiz.why: "One of dull-facultied disposition, whose meditative ease in this very life remains genuinely susceptible to relapse." Master Cháng Bǎi: the dull-facultied arhat's concentration can be lost, but not the noble path.

quiz.q: How many varieties of time-liberated arhat does Venerable Miào Jìng count?
options: five: retrogressing, contemplating, guarding, abiding, advancing
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: there are five varieties here — retrogressing, contemplating, guarding, abiding, and advancing.

quiz.q: What is a wisdom-liberated practitioner, and on what concentration does Master Cháng Bǎi say they rely?
options: outflows exhausted, eight liberations not yet realised; relying on access concentration up to the absorptions, without cessation
quiz.why: "One who has already permanently exhausted every outflow, yet has not yet fully realised and dwelt within the eight liberations." Master Cháng Bǎi: relying on access concentration up through the four absorptions and three formless attainments, without cessation, they enter reality by the power of wisdom and cut off the affliction-obstruction.

quiz.q: By how many principles are practitioners classified, and what are the first three?
quiz.why: "First, difference of faculty; second, difference of assembly; third, difference of temperament … eleventh, difference of obstruction." Venerable Miào Jìng: practitioners are classified by eleven distinct principles.
